summary: Proceed as a stage-2 rewrite with no companions. Two points need fixing at build time: STAGES 6 cannot hold 2 CTAs/SM, so the deeper-ring branch resolves to STAGES 5; and the batch-only CHUNK rule picks 512 at B=32, where tail quantization is already about 3%, rather than at B=16, where it is about 15%. Before any CHUNK=512 run, the in-run per-config kernel-A timings should decide which sub-change is kept.
justification: The target is real. Kernel A is 93-96% of the replaced time (112.0 us at B=16, 249.5 us at B=32 in job e789032128df4291) against KV floors of about 63 and 126 us, which is 1.9-2.05x the floor. The ~95/189 us milestone (3.5 TB/s on a 128-B-row page-1 gather on H200) is physically reachable. The three mechanisms are much weaker than the target. (a) Shared-memory arithmetic from the stage-1 constants: ring 4x16 KB = 65536, idx 2x1024x4 = 8192, q 2048, acc_s 16384, ml 512, seq/pre 528, about 93.2 KB in total. STAGES 6 is about 126 KB, above the 113 KB limit, so 2 CTAs/SM cannot hold and the rule always lands on STAGES 5 (about 109.6 KB; 2x(107+1 KB) = 216 KB fits within 228 KB). Bytes in flight per SM rise from 3x16x2 = 96 KB to 4x16x2 = 128 KB (+33%). But 96 KB x 132 SMs is already about 12.7 MB in flight chip-wide, well above HBM bandwidth x latency even at 2 us, so pure latency-bound starvation is not demonstrated. The 2.6-2.9 TB/s may instead come from the per-tile __syncthreads across 8 warps, the item-end merge barrier, cp.async issue rate (four 16-B cp.async per thread per tile plus the index gather), or gather sector efficiency. (b) The 'agentic tail at B=32' story contradicts the numbers. Items are fixed 1024-token chunks dealt round-robin over a 264-CTA grid, so imbalance is just ceil/mean of items per CTA. B=32 has about 2.36M tokens, about 2300 items, about 8.7 per CTA: max/mean about 9/8.7, roughly 3% loss. B=16 has about 1.18M tokens, about 1150 items, about 4.4 per CTA: max/mean about 5/4.4, roughly 15% loss. B=16 has the worse tail yet the higher bandwidth (2.9 vs 2.6 TB/s), so the B=32 shortfall is something else. Candidates: the combine/workspace, L2 thrash from 32 page-table rows, or per-item overhead. The batch-only rule (512 when batch >= 24) applies the smaller chunk where it helps least and skips the shape where it helps most, and it doubles item-end merges, ws partial writes (about 4.6K x 4 KB, about 19 MB extra at B=32) and combine reads (combine already 8-9 us). (c) Prefetching the next item's page indices two items ahead buys nothing: with one-ahead issue at tile 0 there are already 16 tiles (8 at CHUNK 512) of lead. It also silently requires idx_s to grow to [3][CHUNK] (+4 KB, putting STAGES 5 at about 113.7 KB, which still fits 2/SM but only just), or k&1 buffer reuse races. Weakest link: no profile evidence shows kernel A is limited by bytes in flight or by tail; the M3 gain (17-22 us at B=16, 55-60 us at B=32) is asserted from bandwidth targets rather than derived from a measured bottleneck. Expected directions are otherwise consistent with TASK.md: only full decode_16/32 (weight 16 each) are gated, and every other shape is a valid control.
confounders: full-decode-splitkv-restack-on-pdl (running, restack: conflicts, not landed): this is the actual base. Kernel A's stage-1 times (112.0/249.5 us) were measured on the pre-dense-chain base. If the hand-merged restack moves kernel A (stream, PDL ordering, workspace alloc), the 'old config' reference changes. Use the restack run's own profile and the in-run old-vs-new CUDA-event print as the reference, not the e789 numbers.

small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (gain, master): T<=32 includes decode_16/32. Its PDL chain wraps the qkv/o GEMMs around attention. If kernel A or the combine sits inside a griddepcontrol chain, launch overlap changes, and the shape delta can move without kernel A changing. Judge on kernel A's own us in profile top_kernels, not the shape median.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched (neutral, master): it defines the incumbent being replaced (paired FA3 + pad/unpad) on exactly these shapes. That affects only the incumbent baseline for M2, not this stage's delta, which is splitkv stage 1 vs stage 2.

stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1 / marlin-block-m-cap-16 (master): MoE-side, after attention. Not causal for kernel A, but Marlin swings ±20-40 us between single profiles on byte-identical paths (REWRITE_READ caveat). A shape-level delta of ±20-40 us at full decode_16/32 is uninterpretable from the headline alone.
interference: No companions. This is kind: rewrite stage 2, judged on kernel A's own us against the incumbent and the floor, and none of the landed hypotheses touches kernel A's code path, so an ab-revert would not disambiguate anything. The real attribution risk is internal: three bundled sub-changes (STAGES 5, CHUNK 512 at batch >= 24, two-ahead index prefetch) could cancel each other. That is best resolved in-run at zero check cost. The change already prints kernel-A CUDA-event time for old vs new configs at B=16/32; extend that print to cover each sub-change alone: (S4,C1024), (S5,C1024), (S4,C512), (S5,C512), and two-ahead on/off at the chosen config, at B=16 and B=32 on the self-check synthetic lengths at realistic about 74K average context. Then pick the per-batch winner on device from those timings, as long as the choice comes from batch only. A separate okc control run would cost a check to learn what a 50 ms prepare-time sweep already shows. Caveat: prepare-time timings run with warm L2 and synthetic page tables, so they rank configs but do not reproduce the judge's cold-L2 numbers.
rules_flags: The CHUNK selection must stay a function of config (batch) and shapes only. The 'total KV tokens / (2 x SMs)' clause must not read cache_seqlens on the host (that would be a host sync and branching on input values inside the graph). The text says 'decide from batch', so build it that way and delete the token-count clause.
max_chunks / workspace size must be derived from page_table.shape[1] and the chosen CHUNK (a shape), as in stage 1. Keep the torch.empty allocation shape-only.

Every-key: with CHUNK 512 the partial last chunk and zero-length chunks must still be masked rather than skipped. The self-check must cover a request whose length is an exact multiple of 512 but not of 1024, and one shorter than 512.
No precision issue: FP8 E4M3 queries, FP8 KV widened to f16, fp32 accumulation and partials are unchanged from stage 1.
open_questions: Why is B=32 kernel-A bandwidth (2.6 TB/s) lower than B=16 (2.9 TB/s) when B=32's round-robin tail quantization is better (about 3% vs about 15%)? If a per-batch cost such as the item_of prefix walk, page-table L2 footprint or ws writes is responsible, neither a deeper ring nor CHUNK 512 addresses it.
Is CHUNK 512 better applied at B=16 (items/CTA 4.4 -> 8.7, max/mean 1.15 -> about 1.03) than at B=32? The batch-only rule currently has it backwards relative to the quantization argument.

Does the two-ahead index prefetch get a third idx buffer ([3][CHUNK])? Without one it races with the k&1 double buffer. With one, STAGES 5 + CHUNK 1024 is about 113.7 KB per CTA. That still fits 2 CTAs/SM (about 229 KB including the 1 KB per-block reserve is borderline against the 228 KB SM limit), so verify cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor == 2 and print it.
STAGES 6 cannot fit 2 CTAs/SM with the current layout (about 126 KB). Should it be dropped from the build, or should acc_s (16 KB) be aliased onto a ring stage at item end to make 6 stages fit?
Is full-decode-splitkv-restack-on-pdl's measured kernel-A time close to the stage-1 112.0/249.5 us? If the restack itself moved kernel A, re-derive the expected savings before reading this run.
